summary: The current queue attributes the stop to cmd.c:parse and the generic repeat path, but the actual first cause is the JavaScript rhack() count guard rejecting the # command before doextcmd() can dispatch #wizgenesis. C keeps the parsed count on #, wiz_genesis() consumes it in create_particular_parse() as monster quantity, returns ECMD_OK, and rhack() resets multi before any moveloop repeat.

source.branch: A positive parsed multi reaches the #/doextcmd row. That row must dispatch first; for #wizgenesis, read.c:create_particular_parse consumes 1+gm.multi as quantity, wiz_genesis returns ECMD_OK, and rhack resets command variables. The generic refusal currently runs before the # dispatch.
callers: allmain.c:moveloop_core() invokes cmd.c:rhack() to read the command. This case returns ECMD_OK from the selected #wizgenesis handler, so rhack() clears multi and the repeat branch is not reached.
dependencies: cmd.c:parse() initializes gm.multi from the count (5142-5144); its current JavaScript port reproduces this state.
cmd.c:doextcmd() resolves the full extended command and calls its selected handler (493-519); current JavaScript doextcmd() already dispatches the command.
wizcmds.c:wiz_genesis() calls create_particular() and returns ECMD_OK (201-214); current JavaScript handler is already implemented.
read.c:create_particular_parse() derives quantity from 1+gm.multi when no explicit quantity appears in the answer (3145); current JavaScript parser already implements it.
cmd.c:reset_cmd_vars() clears gm.multi after ECMD_OK; current JavaScript # result path already resets it.
